## Explicit conditional provenance; not the old strict promise

This proposed contract selects ordinary trusted product/observer/Bash/env
bootstrap. It assumes the product and the source-received observation
machinery perform their declared ordinary launches and readings. That
includes the root observation tools and initial interpreter/import bootstrap
which precede an internal receipt check. This is an explicit trust boundary,
not a measurement, inherited-environment audit or complete OS-startup trace.

The original product_startup requirement remains unsatisfied and immutable.
The available interface does not independently establish the product shell's
effective inherited BASH_ENV/ENV/SHELLOPTS/BASHOPTS, exported functions, LD_*
and other applicable startup influences. The list is illustrative, not a
complete environment closure. A later ENV8 or parent initial-environ snapshot
cannot supply this missing fact. This derivative withdraws that strong claim
only for its new, independently reviewed conditional interface; it does not
rename the old requirement and mark it met.

The claimed evidence is limited to independently received finite file/
configuration keys and discrete downstream ENV8, flags, maps, modules, ABI,
native/session and before/after observations, conditional on the stated trust
boundary. There is no guarantee against malicious/hidden earlier startup
effects, escaped writers, continuous loading or races. Unknown received
dependencies and failed observations still cause HOLD. No ambient environment
dump, product setting change or extra process test is included.

Trust is not the independent key receipt. Root must still receive the exact
finite source/interpreter/native/configuration bootstrap key before each
author runtime-only probe. Before the operational Node/tool entry, a different
independently received full key, all fourteen-field descriptors and current
before/after observations remain mandatory. Root observations rely openly on
ordinary trusted tools; no recursive executor is introduced to attest its own
bootstrap. Probe observations cannot retrospectively justify unreceived
pre-probe imports or replace pre-Node/tool keys.

Every new binding/authorization and proposed result carries the same fixed
provenance object: schema=p212-trusted-product-boundary-v1,
assumption=ordinary_product_observer_bash_env_bootstrap,
product_startup_attested=false (literal boolean), and
claim=finite_received_keys_and_discrete_downstream_observations.
This is a declared model, never a receipt or acceptance by itself.
